newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS STARS CLEARED OF SEX ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS STARS CLEARED OF SEX ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS.

text.p: Dallas Cowboys stars Michael Irvin and Erik Williams were cleared of sex assault allegations on Friday after the woman who accused them of raping her at gunpoint admitted she had lied, police said.
Police spokesman Ed Spencer said the 23-year-old woman withdrew her allegations, and that there was no case against either Irvin or Williams.

The woman had accused Irvin of holding a gun against her head and threatening to kill her while Williams and a third, unidentified man raped her on top of a pool table inside Williams' home on December 29.
She also alleged the men videotaped the assault and snorted cocaine.

"We have determined conclusively that the allegations are not true and that a sexual assault did not take place," Spencer said. "Additionally, we have determined that Michael Irvin was not present at any time during this incident."
Irvin, 30, and Williams, 28, had flatly denied the accusations from the start. Irvin said he had not been at Williams' home in 18 months.
Spencer said the Cowboys players had told the truth and that misdemeanor charges might now be filed against the woman.

Irvin, one of the National Football League's premier wide receivers, was a key member of the Dallas teams that won three of the last four Super Bowls. The defending Super Bowl champions were eliminated from the title hunt last Sunday when they were defeated by the second-year Carolina Panthers 26-17 in a National Football Conference (NFC) playoff game.

The rape allegation was the latest in a string of ugly scandals to rock the Cowboys team over the last two years, but Irvin's lawyer Royce West said he hoped Irvin would be able to overcome the damage done to his reputation.
West also said the legal battle was not yet over, hinting at possible legal action against the woman, the police or the media.

Irvin is currently on four years probation after pleading no contest to felony cocaine possession charges last year. Irvin was suspended by the NFL for the first five games of the season, but had he been arrested on aggravated sexual assault charges, he could have had his probation revoked and been sent to jail.
But the woman recanted her allegations before police filed formal charges against the Cowboys players.
